literal: His title was advanced to General Who Suppresses the South.
idiomatic: His rank was advanced to general who suppresses the south.

literal: In the third year of Wuding he led troops to lift the siege of Xiang Province.
idiomatic: In the third year of Wuding he led troops to raise the siege of Xiang Province.

literal: He was frequently sent on missions to the Rouran.
idiomatic: He was repeatedly dispatched on diplomatic missions to the Rouran.

literal: He again followed in the attack on Yubi and was granted seven hundred bolts of silk together with hats and clothing.
idiomatic: He again followed the attack on Yubi and was rewarded with seven hundred bolts of silk, hats, and clothing.

literal: In the fifth year he garrisoned the five cities at River Bridge.
idiomatic: In the fifth year he was stationed at the five cities of River Bridge.

literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, Yan attacked the bandits of Chen Commandery and captured Kudi Helai under Jing's command, together with falsely appointed Governor Zheng Daohe, Yanzhou Inspector Wang Yanxia, Mobile Circuit Commissioner Di Chang, and others; more than a hundred were captured and beheaded.
idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled, Murong Yan struck the rebel forces in Chen Commandery and captured Kudi Helai of Hou Jing's following, together with the falsely appointed governor Zheng Daohe, Yanzhou inspector Wang Yanxia, mobile circuit commissioner Di Chang, and others — more than a hundred heads taken in all.

literal: Wheeling his army to Xiangcheng, he again captured Jing's falsely appointed Inspector Xin Guang and Cai Zun, together with two thousand of their subordinates.
idiomatic: Marching on Xiangcheng, he again seized Hou Jing's pseudo-inspector Xin Guang and Cai Zun, together with two thousand of their troops.

literal: In the sixth year he was appointed Governor of Qiao Province; he repeatedly won distinction in battle and brought many to submit.
idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made governor of Qiao Province; he won repeated victories and brought many defectors over.

literal: In the seventh year he was again appointed Governor of Jiao Province.
idiomatic: In the seventh year he was made governor of Jiao Province.

literal: At the start of Tianbao he was appointed Opening-Establishment Honor Equal to the Three Dukes.
idiomatic: At the start of Tianbao he was granted opening-establishment honor equal to the three dukes.

literal: In the sixth year, Liang Minister over the Masses Lu Fahé, Equal-in-Rank Song Chihui, and others led their followers in submitting from within Ying Province city.
idiomatic: In the sixth year, Liang minister over the masses Lu Fahé, equal-in-rank Song Chihui, and others brought their followers over from within the walls of Ying city.

literal: At that time Prince of Qinghe Yue commanded troops on the river; he gathered the armies in council and said: "The city lies beyond the river; hearts there are still recalcitrant. One must have both talent and stratagem, with loyalty and courage surpassing other men — only such a one can receive this charge."
idiomatic: At that time Prince of Qinghe Yue had troops on the Yangzi and called the commanders together. "The city stands beyond the river," he said, "and hearts there are still hard to win. It will take a man who combines talent with stratagem, whose loyalty and courage outmatch all others — only such a man can hold this trust."

literal: All together recommended Yan.
idiomatic: The assembly unanimously pointed to Murong Yan.

literal: Yue agreed and thereupon dispatched him to garrison Ying city.
idiomatic: Yue assented and sent Yan to hold Ying city.

literal: As soon as he entered, Liang Grand Commander-in-Chief Hou Zhen and Ren Yue led land and river forces and suddenly arrived beneath the walls.
idiomatic: Hardly had he entered when Liang grand commander Hou Zhen and Ren Yue swept up by land and water to the foot of the walls.

literal: Yan met each threat with appropriate defense; Zhen and the others could not take the city.
idiomatic: Murong Yan answered each threat as it came; Zhen and his fellows could not break him.

literal: They also constructed a reed barrier several li long on Parrot Isle upstream to block the shipping lanes.
idiomatic: Upstream at Parrot Isle they built a reed boom several li long to choke off the river route.

literal: Communications with the outside were cut off; the city's defense hung alone; the crowd grew fearful — Yan guided them with loyalty and righteousness, and also soothed and settled them.
idiomatic: Cut off from the world, the garrison clung to an isolated city, and fear spread through the ranks. Yan led them with talk of loyalty and duty, and won them back with kindness until they steadied.

literal: Within the city there was already a spirit shrine, popularly called the City God; both public and private made prayers there.
idiomatic: The city already held a shrine to what people called the City God; officials and commoners alike prayed there.

literal: Thereupon, following the hearts of the officers and soldiers, they went together to pray, hoping to obtain invisible aid.
idiomatic: Reading the mood of his troops, he led them in common prayer, hoping for protection from beyond the veil.

literal: In a moment a rushing wind suddenly arose; startled waves surged and swept away the reed barrier.
idiomatic: In an instant a tearing wind sprang up; waves roared and tore the reed boom apart.

literal: Yue again joined iron chains in a continuous barrier; the blockade grew tighter still.
idiomatic: Ren Yue linked iron chains in a fresh barrier; the blockade tightened.

literal: Yan again prayed with them together; wind and waves startled the night and once more broke it apart — this happened again and again.
idiomatic: Yan prayed with them again; that night wind and waves rose in fury and snapped the chains once more — and so it went, again and again.

literal: The people of the city rejoiced greatly and took it for divine merit.
idiomatic: The city erupted in joy and called it the work of the gods.

literal: Zhen shifted his army to the north of the city, built palisades and set up camps, and burned the wards — every estate was destroyed.
idiomatic: Zhen shifted north of the walls, threw up palisades and camps, and burned the suburbs until nothing was left standing.

literal: Yue commanded more than ten thousand fighting men, each bearing siege engines; south of the city he set up camps and joined forces north and south.
idiomatic: Ren Yue brought more than ten thousand warriors with siege gear and pitched camp south of the city, closing a pincer from north and south.

literal: Yan then led infantry and cavalry out of the city in a fierce charge, routed them greatly, and captured more than five hundred men.
idiomatic: Yan led infantry and cavalry out in a furious sally, broke them utterly, and took more than five hundred prisoners.

literal: Earlier Ying city had been low-lying; its earth was loose and the walls crumbling — Yan rebuilt the parapets and raised many great towers.
idiomatic: Ying had been a low, ramshackle place with walls of crumbling earth. Yan rebuilt the ramparts and raised tall fighting towers.

literal: He also built war vessels; land and river forces were fully equipped, and labor never paused.
idiomatic: He built warships too; land and river were readied for war, and the work crews never rested.

literal: Xiao Xun again led fifty thousand men, joined armies with Zhen and Yue, and came by night to attack.
idiomatic: Xiao Xun mustered fifty thousand more, combined with Zhen and Yue, and struck at night.

literal: Yan and his officers and soldiers fought with all their strength through the night; at dawn Yue and the others withdrew.
idiomatic: Yan and his men fought through the night; at first light, Ren Yue and the rest fell back.

literal: Pursuing, he beheaded Zhen's fierce general Zhang Baishi; Zhen offered a thousand in gold to ransom him — Yan refused.
idiomatic: In pursuit he cut down Zhen's champion Zhang Baishi. Zhen offered a thousand in gold for the head — Yan would not take it.

literal: In the fifth month of summer Zhen, Yue, and the others again joined forces and assaulted the siege with their entire host.
idiomatic: In the fifth month Zhen and Ren Yue joined again and threw every man they had at the walls.

literal: Food in the city was scarce; grain convoys were cut off with no remedy — they could only boil pagoda tree, paper mulberry leaves, ramie roots, duckweed, kudzu, mugwort, and the like, together with boots, leather belts, sinews and horns, and eat them.
idiomatic: Provisions ran low; grain could not get through. With no other recourse they boiled pagoda bark, mulberry leaves, ramie root, duckweed, kudzu, mugwort — boots, belts, sinew and horn — and ate whatever would cook.

literal: When a man died, they immediately took his flesh, divided it with fire, and ate — leaving only the bones.
idiomatic: When a man died, they cut his flesh, cooked it, and shared it out, leaving only the bones.

literal: Yet Yan still announced orders to officers and soldiers: rewards given in faith, punishments surely carried out; sweetness shared, bitterness shared — life and death together.
idiomatic: Even then Yan kept discipline among his men: promised rewards he paid, promised punishments he delivered; whatever sweetness or bitterness remained, he shared it — life and death alike.

literal: From the first month to the sixth, none wavered in will.
idiomatic: From the first month through the sixth, not one man broke faith.

literal: Later, when Xiao Fangzhi was enthroned, he dispatched envoys requesting peace.
idiomatic: Later Xiao Fangzhi came to the throne and sent envoys suing for peace.

literal: Emperor Wenxuan, because the city lay on the southern bank of the river and holding it was inconvenient, issued an edict recalling it.
idiomatic: Gao Yang, judging that a city south of the river was too hard to hold, ordered the garrison withdrawn.

literal: Yan looked upon the emperor and grieved beyond bearing.
idiomatic: When Yan saw the emperor again, grief overwhelmed him.

literal: The emperor called him forward, took his hand, held Yan's beard and side whiskers, removed his hat to look at his hair, and sighed long.
idiomatic: The emperor called him forward, clasped his hand, lifted Yan's beard, took off his hat to see how his hair had turned, and sighed a long while.

literal: He said to Yan: "Looking at your face, I no longer recognize you. Loyal heroes since antiquity — could any surpass this?"
idiomatic: He said to Yan, "Looking at you, I would not know you. Among the loyal and fierce of every age — who has surpassed this?"

literal: Yan replied: "Your servant relied on Your Majesty's august power and attained my humble loyalty; I did not bow to those petty fellows and again behold the sacred countenance."
idiomatic: Yan answered, "I leaned on Your Majesty's majesty to keep my poor pledge — I did not bow to those whelps, and here I stand before you again."

literal: Though I die tonight, in death I will have no regret."
idiomatic: Even if I die tonight, I will go without regret."

literal: The emperor exclaimed praise without end.
idiomatic: The emperor praised him again and again.

literal: He was appointed Governor of Zhao Province; his rank as Baron was advanced to Duke, and he was granted one thousand bolts of silk and a hundred thousand cash.
idiomatic: Murong Yan was made governor of Zhao Province, raised from baron to duke, and given a thousand bolts of silk and a hundred thousand cash.

literal: Among Erzhu generals who after the righteous banner was raised submitted and achieved merit, Wuwei Dieshele and Dai's Fan Shele also reached eminence.
idiomatic: Among Erzhu commanders who came over after the righteous standard was raised and won distinction — Wuwei Dieshele and Fan Shele of Dai also rose to high rank.

literal: Dieshele in youth followed Erzhu Rong as army commander and army leader; later he was Registered-Tribal Commander of Xihe.
idiomatic: Dieshele followed Erzhu Rong from youth as army commander and army leader, and later served as registered-tribal commander of Xihe.

literal: When Erzhu Zhao was defeated, he led his host to submit to the Grand Ancestor and was appointed General Who Stabilizes the West and Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao fell, he brought his troops to Gao Huan and was made general who stabilizes the west and grand master of the golden seal and purple ribbon.

literal: As a commander he served under Hou Jing and defeated Helü Sheng at Rang city.
idiomatic: Serving under Hou Jing as commander, he defeated Helü Sheng at Rang.

literal: He again with the generals suppressed and pacified the three provinces of Qing, Yan, and Jing, and was appointed General Who Stabilizes the West and Governor of Ying Province.
idiomatic: With other generals he pacified Qing, Yan, and Jing provinces and was made general who stabilizes the west and governor of Ying Province.

literal: At the start of Tianbao he was enfeoffed Duke of Hanzhong Commandery.
idiomatic: At the start of Tianbao he was enfeoffed duke of Hanzhong Commandery.

literal: Later he fell in battle in Guanzhong.
idiomatic: Later he fell in battle in Guanzhong.

literal: Fan Shele had martial skill; his strength surpassed other men.
idiomatic: Fan Shele was skilled in arms, with strength beyond ordinary men.

literal: At the end of Wei he followed Cui Xuan, Li Chong, and others on punitive campaigns with merit and was appointed army leader.
idiomatic: In the late Wei he followed Cui Xuan and Li Chong on campaigns, won merit, and was made army leader.

literal: Later he entered Erzhu Rong's army; he frequently had military merit and was appointed commander.
idiomatic: Later he entered Erzhu Rong's ranks, won repeated victories, and was made commander.

literal: Later he followed Erzhu Zhao in defeating Bu Fan at Liangdu.
idiomatic: He followed Erzhu Zhao to break Bu Fan at Liangdu.

literal: When the Grand Ancestor raised the righteous banner, he abandoned Zhao and returned to Xindu.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan raised the righteous banner, he abandoned Zhao and joined him at Xindu.

literal: Following the Grand Ancestor he defeated Zhao at Guang'a and Hanling, both with merit, and was granted the title Baron of Pingshu.
idiomatic: He followed Gao Huan in defeating Zhao at Guang'a and Hanling, and for merit on both fields was enfeoffed baron of Pingshu.

literal: Whenever he followed on campaign, he often won victories.
idiomatic: On every campaign he fought, he often carried the day.

literal: He was appointed Grand Commander of the Chancellor's Left Wing.
idiomatic: He was made grand commander of the chancellor's left wing.

literal: Soon he was sent out as Governor of Eastern Yong Province.
idiomatic: Soon he was sent out as governor of Eastern Yong Province.

literal: When the Heir Apparent succeeded to affairs he was enfeoffed Marquis of Pingshu County and appointed Equal-in-Rank.
idiomatic: When Gao Cheng took up power he was enfeoffed marquis of Pingshu County and made equal-in-rank.

literal: In the Tianbao era his rank was advanced to opening-establishment.
idiomatic: In the Tianbao era he was promoted to opening-establishment rank.

literal: There was also Kudí Fulian of Dai, styled Zhongshan; in youth for martial capacity he served Erzhu Rong and reached Direct Attendant General.
idiomatic: There was also Kudí Fulian of Dai, styled Zhongshan — a man who from youth served Erzhu Rong for his martial worth and rose to direct attendant general.

literal: Later he followed the Grand Ancestor in establishing righteousness and was granted the title Baron of Sheqiu.
idiomatic: Later he followed Gao Huan in raising the revolt and was enfeoffed baron of Sheqiu.

literal: When the Heir Apparent assisted in government, he was transferred to Martial Guard General.
idiomatic: When Gao Cheng guided affairs of state, he was made martial guard general.

literal: At the start of Tianbao he held honor equal to the three dukes.
idiomatic: At the start of Tianbao he held honor equal to the three dukes.

literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Governor of Zheng Province; soon opening-establishment rank was added.
idiomatic: In the fourth year he was made governor of Zheng Province; opening-establishment rank followed shortly after.

literal: Fulian was plain and sincere and diligent in public business.
idiomatic: Fulian was plain-spoken and diligent in office.

literal: When the direct guard posts were vacant, dawn and dusk he did not leave the emperor's side — for this he won notice.
idiomatic: When direct guard duty fell to him, he stayed at the emperor's side from dawn to dusk — and won favor for it.

literal: Mean, stingy, foolish and harsh — he had no art of governing the people.
idiomatic: Yet he was petty, tight-fisted, coarse and cruel, with no gift for civil rule.

literal: When he held provincial office, his sole business was accumulation and extraction.
idiomatic: In provincial office his only business was squeezing the people dry.

literal: By nature he was also harsh and cruel and did not recognize genteel society.
idiomatic: His nature ran harsh and cruel; he had no patience for cultivated men.

literal: Opening-establishment staff officers were mostly genteel clansmen in official dress — Fulian beat them with flails and drove them to build walls.
idiomatic: His opening-establishment aides were mostly men of gentle birth — Fulian flogged them and drove them out to raise walls.

literal: In Wuping he was enfeoffed Prince of Yidu Commandery and appointed Colonel Director of the Army.
idiomatic: In Wuping he was enfeoffed prince of Yidu Commandery and made colonel director of the army.

literal: Soon, together with Prince of Langya Yan, he killed He Shikai and was executed.
idiomatic: Soon, together with Gao Yan, Prince of Langya, he killed He Shikai and paid with his life.

literal: Fulian's household numbered in the hundreds; in midsummer days he rationed them two sheng of storehouse grain, gave no salt or vegetables, and they often showed hunger in their faces.
idiomatic: Fulian kept a household of a hundred mouths. Even in high summer he rationed them two sheng of stored grain apiece, with no salt or greens — hunger showed on every face.

literal: On the winter solstice, kin and friends offered congratulations; his wife set out bean cakes.
idiomatic: On the winter solstice kith and kin came to offer felicitations; his wife served bean cakes.

literal: Fulian asked whence these beans came; his wife replied that she had taken them by division from the horse-feed beans — Fulian flew into a rage; the horse stewards and food keepers were all flogged. Gifts accumulated over years he stored in a separate treasury, sending one maidservant exclusively to keep the keys.
idiomatic: Fulian demanded to know where the beans had come from. His wife confessed she had skimmed them from the horse-feed stores. He flew into a rage and had the stable and pantry stewards flogged. Years of imperial gifts he locked in a separate vault, with a single maid holding the keys.

literal: Whenever he entered the storehouse to inspect, he invariably told wife and children: "These are official goods — you must not use them at will."
idiomatic: Each time he inspected the vault he told his wife and children, "These are state goods. You are not to touch them."

literal: At this time an inventory was made and all was returned to the imperial treasury.
idiomatic: After his execution an inventory was taken and everything went back to the imperial treasury.

literal: The historian writes: When the Grand Ancestor's hegemonic enterprise was first laid, he gathered the brave.
idiomatic: The historian writes: When Gao Huan first laid the foundations of empire, he gathered the brave.

literal: Zhang Qiong and the others, though their discernment fell short of foresight, met the fortune of their time; they raced through martial campaigns with never a day's respite, loyally proclaiming resistance to insult, in accord with the favored design — facing the enemy and securing victory, they deserve mention.
idiomatic: Zhang Qiong and the rest were no prophets — yet fortune favored their hour. They spent their days in the saddle without rest, holding the line with loyal hearts, serving the founding design — and when steel met steel they prevailed. That much deserves record.

literal: Murong Shaozong's military timing and martial stratagem were praised in his age.
idiomatic: Murong Shaozong's grasp of war and martial stratagem won esteem in his own day.

literal: In former days he served the Erzhu, holding fast to loyalty and righteousness; he did not heed Fan Zeng's counsel and in the end met calamity at the Wu River.
idiomatic: Once he served the Erzhu clan and clung to loyalty even past reason — he would not take Fan Zeng's advice, and in the end met his Wu River.

literal: Hou Jing was savage and unruly — no true minister to the Later Sovereign; his final testamentary words truly showed discernment in knowing men.
idiomatic: Hou Jing was savage and untamable — no fit servant for a later sovereign. His dying words showed a clearer eye for men than his living years.

literal: At Hanshan and Guo River — going forth like snapping dry wood; his calculations exhausted, his fortune strange, meeting this calamitous fate — lamentable!
idiomatic: At Hanshan and the Guo River he had gone forth like snapping deadwood — yet fate ran against him, calculations failed, and this bitter end came. Alas!

literal: The encomium says: The hegemonic design was first established; the royal enterprise arose from it.
idiomatic: The encomium says: The hegemonic design was first laid — the royal enterprise grew from that root.

literal: Great are these generals — truly they are meritorious ministers.
idiomatic: Great were these generals — true pillars of merit.

literal: Forever remembering Geng and Jia, without burdening the pure dust.
idiomatic: May they stand forever beside Geng and Jia, unburdened by worldly stain.

literal: The entire text has been collated against the November 1972 first edition of the Book of Northern Qi published by Zhonghua Shuju.
idiomatic: The entire text has been collated against the November 1972 first edition of the Book of Northern Qi published by Zhonghua Shuju.
